_comment: Fitting a lot to the broker's own volume ladder.
round_volume(v, spec) = the largest multiple of volume_step that is
<= v, inside [volume_min, volume_max],
or 0 when no tradeable size fits
DOWN, NEVER UP. This is not a presentational nicety: the lot comes out
of volume_for_risk, which divides a money budget by what the stop costs
per lot. Rounding that result up spends more than the budget - the one
number the trader actually agreed to.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. round_volume finished with round(out, 2), which
hardcoded two decimals instead of taking them from the broker's step.
On a book quoting 0.001 lots that was wrong twice over:
* round_volume(0.001) -> 0.0, so the broker's OWN MINIMUM LOT read as
'no tradeable size'. An off switch nobody asked for.
* round_volume(0.005) -> 0.01, rounded UP, against the docstring and
against the cap. A $10 budget with a stop costing $2000/lot sizes to
0.005 lots; it was sent as 0.01 and risked $20. Double.
* round_volume(0.125) -> 0.12, a silent haircut of a perfectly valid
size.
0.01 is the step on nearly every retail forex book, which is why this
survived: at two decimals the old code and the rule agree exactly. The
step-0.01 cases below are here to keep that true.
Adding a case here is how the rule changes.
